t:
There are authorized to be appropriated, at a rate not to exceed $5,000,000 annually, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act.
This Act may be cited as the “Institute of Inter-American Affairs Act”.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations and gives the Act a short title. There is no tempting reading here: no outside party is consulted, heard, appointed to an advisory body, or given a right to sue, and no rulemaking is authorized. Nothing in it crosses the federal boundary into a federal decision.
fable.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, at a rate not to exceed $5,000,000 annually, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act.

qwen_block.w: This section contains only an authorization of appropriations and a short title citation. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or requirements for state/local involvement mentioned.
qwen_block.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, at a rate not to exceed $5,000,000 annually, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act. This Act may be cited as the “Institute of Inter-American Affairs Act”.

opus.w: This section only authorizes up to $5,000,000 a year in appropriations and gives the Act a short title. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue. The phrase "Inter-American Affairs" in the title is just a name and does not create any process involving outside parties.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The name "Inter-American Affairs" might suggest dealings with foreign governments or outside parties. But this section only authorizes money and gives the Act its short title. No process brings outsiders into a federal decision, so the definition is not met.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard authorization of appropriations clause. It provides funding for the Act but does not establish any mechanism for public participation, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. It involves only the federal government's internal budgetary process.
qwen_chat.s: There are authorized to be appropriated, at a rate not to exceed $5,000,000 annually, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "carrying out this Act" implicitly involves public participation, but the text itself contains no procedural requirements for consultation, hearings, or advisory bodies. It is purely a funding authorization.
